newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Foreigners should take part in VUB sale - Slovak PM.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners should take part in VUB sale - Slovak PM.

text.p: Foreign investors should be allowed to participate in the privatisation of commercial bank VUB, the independent daily Narodna Obroda on Friday quoted Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar as saying.

Meciar also said there are plans to merge VUB, the largest commercial bank, with Slovenska Sporitelna a.s., the country's largest savings bank, "to create a financial institution more competitive in central Europe".
"In the case of privatising VUB, we feel a foreign investor may take a stake in it, which should help the bank be included in the wider international financial network," Meciar told the paper.

He did not elaborate on the size of the potential stake foreigners may be offered in the bank. The state, through the privatisation agency the National Property Fund, holds a 51.9 percent in VUB and a 91.3 percent stake in Sporitelna.
Meciar also criticised parliament's recent approval of a law postponing any bank privatisation until the end of 2003, saying it would slow down the growth of state-controlled banks.
